title: Dual-horizon cycle slotting & capacity rebalancing protocol
creator: Claire Huang
description:
Problem: We frequently face mid-cycle friction where critical runtime reliability or infra work competes with roadmap bets. Current single-horizon planning (one cycle only) lacks a formal buffer and clear rules for mid-cycle reallocation, leading to rushed scope cuts or ad-hoc staffing pulls from other initiatives.

Goal: Define a repeatable, operational 'dual-horizon' protocol for cycle slotting and rebalancing that preserves predictable delivery for committed customer-facing milestones while reserving a clearly defined contingency runway for emergent reliability or enterprise requests. The protocol should reduce last-minute scope churn, make trade-offs transparent, and provide tooling inputs (cycle dashboard signals) to trigger rebalancing.

Scope: This ticket covers the definition of the protocol, initial thresholds and signals, stakeholder responsibilities, an example staffing allocation model, and a short runbook for mid-cycle execution. Implementation and automation (dashboard gating, policy enforcement) are separate follow-ups owned by ENG and Platform.

Deliverables: 
- Written protocol document (this ticket) and short playbook for PMs and Eng leads.
- Example capacity model with FTE-to-point mapping and 3 scenario demos (best-case, baseline, emergency rebalancing).
- Acceptance criteria and handoff notes for engineering (dashboards/alerts) and design (communication templates).
tasks: Draft protocol and terminology: define 'Core Commitment', 'Buffer Lane', 'Surge Pool' and 'Rebalance Window'
Produce capacity model: convert FTE allocations to story points and compute buffer size recommendations (5-15% of cycle capacity depending on org confidence)
Define signals and thresholds: latency/error % increases, oncall escalations, enterprise compliance requests that trigger Rebalance Window
Create decision matrix for scope cuts: customer impact, technical debt risk, dependencies, cross-team effort
Create communication templates: PM -> Eng leads, Exec summary, impacted stakeholders list
Sync with Eng and Design: collect feedback and confirm handoffs to build dashboards/alerts
Publish protocol to Confluence and link to cycle kickoff templates
acceptance_criteria: Protocol doc published in Confluence with clear definitions and step-by-step runbook
Capacity model includes examples for 6-team org and single-product 10-engineer team showing buffer calculations
Decision matrix contains explicit scoring rubric and a pre-approved minimal-scope cut (MVP+maintenance) template
Stakeholder approval recorded: Eng lead, Head of Product, Design lead, SRE manager
Handoff ticket(s) created for engineering to implement two dashboard signals: service-level error increase >25% over baseline and oncall paging frequency doubling vs rolling 30d
risks: Teams may treat Buffer Lane as 'free' capacity and fill it with stretch scope unless governance is enforced
Insufficient baseline telemetry will cause false positives or missed signals; engineering support required to tune thresholds
Political pushback from PMs if buffer reduces headline committed features; communication and OKR alignment needed

notes: Example capacity model (excerpt): For a 10-engineer team, assume velocity 30 pts/cycle -> Core Commitment 26 pts, Buffer Lane 2-3 pts (8-10%), Surge Pool reserve 2 pts. Rebalance rule: if Buffer consumed >50% by emergent work within first 2 weeks, trigger cross-team surge and executive review.
communication_plan: Pre-kickoff: share protocol with all PMs and Eng leads. Kickoff: 15m at cycle planning to confirm buffer size. Mid-cycle: if trigger hits, send 'Rebalance Notice' template to execs + affected customers. Post-cycle: retrospective note capturing buffer use and lessons
examples: Scenario A (Baseline): Team reserves 8% buffer; no emergent events; deliver 95% of committed features; leftover buffer returned to org pool

Scenario B (Reliability Event Week 2): Error rate spikes 40%; trigger Rebalance Window; Surge Pool provides 1 FTE-equivalent; non-critical feature 'rich-preview' is trimmed to 'core-preview' per decision matrix

Scenario C (Enterprise Compliance Request): Unexpected audit requires 3 engineer-weeks; pre-approved partial scope cut: postpone non-customer-critical integration and shift Buffer Lane plus Surge Pool
